purpose: A signal badge that nearly every creator in a domain carries has stopped describing the creator and started describing the field. Rule 17: handle it once, on the category page, and leave the per-creator badge to do the work it can still do — who discloses, who is selling the specific thing they are advising on, and who is merely hosting.

marketing.reviewWhen: marketing reaches 4 creators and the signal can be measured
marketing.note: Almost every marketing creator listed here has a commercial interest in the field they are explaining. That is the shape of the supply rather than a run of bad apples: the independent practitioners in this field publish in newsletters and blogs, and most of the video that exists is hosted by companies selling the tools. Read the commercial-interest badge for what it can still separate — who discloses the conflict, who is selling the specific thing they are advising you to do, and who is only hosting an outside practitioner's thinking on their own platform.
marketing.provenance: Stated from the marketing domain pass, not from a measurement: with 2 creators the percentage would be arithmetic, not evidence. Flagged here so it is re-checked rather than assumed.

fitness.note: Nearly everyone listed here coaches people and sells a program. The first is our own inclusion rule — we do not list fitness explainers who have never trained anyone — so it separates these creators from the wider internet, not from each other. The second is the field: paid coaching and programming is how most credible fitness educators are funded, so selling one is not in itself a mark against a creator. What still varies is whether the free material stands on its own without the purchase, and the per-creator notes say so.

programming.note: Everyone listed here writes code outside of teaching it, and most sell a course or a paid track. The first is our own inclusion rule and distinguishes nobody within the domain. The second is close to universal among independent programming educators, so treat it as the default rather than as a warning. The question worth asking is whether the free videos are complete enough to learn from without buying anything, which is what the per-creator notes address.

productivity.note: Everyone listed here runs the system they teach, and most sell a course, an app or a book built on it. Productivity is unusually self-referential this way: the product often is the method, so the incentive to present one method as more general than it is comes built into the domain. The badge is therefore the norm here; the per-creator notes name what each person sells and how hard they push it.

creativity.note: Almost everyone listed here makes the work they teach, because that is what we required in order to list them at all. The badge marks our floor rather than anything that sets these creators apart. Course selling, by contrast, is split roughly down the middle in this domain, so that badge still tells you something.

tech.note: Almost everyone listed here works in the field they cover — our own inclusion rule, so it does not separate these creators from each other. The badges that still vary in this domain are sponsorship and commercial interest, and those are worth reading on the individual cards.

money.note: Almost everyone listed here works in finance rather than only commenting on it, because that is what we required to list them. The badge marks our floor. In this domain the badges that actually distinguish creators are formal credentials, whether claims are contested, and whether the creator's firm sells the products being discussed.

career.note: Almost everyone listed here has hired, managed or recruited rather than only writing about it — our inclusion rule, not a distinction between them. Course selling is the badge that still varies here, and roughly half of these creators carry it.

mindset.note: Most creators listed here practise what they teach, which is our own inclusion rule rather than a difference between them. In this domain the badge that matters most is whether someone holds a clinical credential — about half do — and that one is on the individual cards.

open.question: Is sells-course near-universal in business the way it is in fitness, productivity and programming?
open.blockedBy: business has 2 creators. Below the 4-creator minimum the percentage is arithmetic rather than evidence — 1 of 2 is 50% and means nothing.
